summary: The account_user table contains 245 rows with 244 distinct non‑NULL last_name values, meaning one duplicate exists. Adding a unique constraint on last_name would require either changing that row's value (prohibited by the "pre-existing rows' values must not change" rule) or allowing the duplicate to remain, both of which break the goal. The closest workable plan is a direct deploy_new with migration "apply" followed by retire_old; the runner will record that the new version's migration fails because of the duplicate.
revision_notes: The plan was originally rejected because the database has a duplicate last_name value (Cook). No SQL stages can resolve this without altering pre‑existing rows, which is disallowed. Therefore the plan remains a reject; the deploy_new stage will fail as shown in the dry‑run, evidence of the constraint conflict.

stages.description: Retire the old Saleor version after the new version is running.
